one_month_reasoning: The window (to 2026-11-12) contains Q3 2026 results and the Q4 guide on Oct 29 before the European open (ST release, 2026-10-05). Q3 was guided to $3.70B +/-350bp and 37.0% GM; management already said Q4 revenue should exceed $4B, so the swing factor is the Q4 number and GM vs a street that sits slightly above (FY26 consensus $14.43B implies ~$4.1B Q4), plus any 2027 datacenter commentary. ST's recent earnings weeks were large moves (weekly closes: $62.06 -> $51.54 the week of the Q2 2026 report in July 2026, $29.25 -> $24.86 the week of the Q3 2025 report), and the stock just fell ~13% in the week to Oct 13 with no company news (buyback and CEO-reappointment 6-Ks only). No edge on the sign: the stock already de-rated 40% from its June high, which lowers the bar, but the July pattern of guiding below consensus argues the other way. I center at roughly today's price (P(>=49.57)=0.48) with monthly vol ~16.5% (61%/3.5 = 17%) and a 25% weight on a wider (25%) earnings-jump component for fat tails.

comps_summary.our_multiple_vs_peers: 19x NTM after-SBC GAAP EPS at the horizon = peer median 18.3x adjusted ~+5% for basis (peers' non-GAAP EPS excludes SBC at ADI/MCHP/ON/MPWR/ALGM; STM's costed SBC is ~1.6% of revenue). Inside the range, roughly at the median.
comps_summary.premium_discount_justification: No premium or discount taken. Arguments for a premium (2027 EPS growth ~+99% from a trough, datacenter optics >$2B) are offset by structurally lower margins and returns than TXN/ADI (FY25 GAAP operating margin 1.5% vs CMD target 22-24%), a loss-making SiC/P&D segment (-21.4% margin Q2 26), 17.7% Apple concentration, and a history of pushing out long-range targets (2027 $20B moved to 2030). Higher growth is already in the EPS we apply the multiple to, so a median multiple avoids double counting.

thesis_break_reason: Below ~$34 (about -31%, under the post-Q2 crash lows ~$48 by a wide margin and back to March 2026 levels) the market would be pricing FY27 EPS near $1.8 at ~19x, i.e. the 2027 recovery and the >$2B datacenter ramp failing or a renewed down-cycle with gross margin stuck in the mid-30s. That is a fundamental miss vs the Q4 >$4B guide and the reaffirmed $18B 2028 target, not ordinary 61%-vol noise.

reverse_dcf_check: The engine reports the 19x horizon P/E implies a 9.1% WACC on our cash flows (vs our 11.3%), i.e. at 11.3% the multiple needs more than our FY29 21% GAAP EBIT margin and 3% terminal growth: roughly a sustained ~24-25% margin (top of the CMD 2027-28 band, still below the >30% 2030 ambition) or ~4.5% long-run growth. Plausible only if the reshaping savings land and SiC breaks even; the probability-weighted long-dated risks (~-$8/share in total) are why we stop at the peer-median multiple rather than a premium and keep FY29 margin below the CMD band, which is also why the DCF ($41) sits below the multiple leg ($55).

sbc_treatment.note: GAAP EBIT/EPS after SBC (FY25 SBC $193M = 1.6% of revenue). ST's own non-GAAP EPS does not add back SBC; peers' non-GAAP EPS mostly does, so the peer median P/E was lifted ~5% to match STM's after-SBC basis. Share count roughly flat (-0.3%/yr): buybacks offset SBC vesting.

reasoning: Primary-document lane. ST is in an analog/MCU upcycle: revenue troughed at $11.8B in FY25 (operating margin 1.5%), rebounded to $3.10B Q1 and $3.49B Q2 2026, with Q3 guided at $3.70B/37% GM and Q4 'above $4B'; book-to-bill ~2, inventory down to 126 days, datacenter >$1B in 2026 and 'well above $2B' in 2027, $18B 2028 revenue target reaffirmed. Against that: the stock fell from $81 (June) to $49.57 after a Q3 guide below consensus, GAAP margins remain low (Q2 GAAP EBIT 5.4%), P&D/SiC loses money, Apple is 17.7% of revenue and long-range targets have slipped before. Filings show capex at the top of $2.0-2.2B, an 18.1% tax rate, net cash $2.0B, and dilution contained (new converts struck at $120-122; Tranche B settled net-share from treasury). I model GAAP (after SBC) revenue $14.3B/$16.8B/$18.3B and EBIT margin 7.5%/15.5%/19% for 2026-28, value at 19x NTM EPS (peer median 18.3x on 10 analog/power/MCU peers, basis-adjusted) blended 70/30 with an 11.3%-WACC DCF -> $51.1, ~3% above spot; street average target $75 is evidence of optimism, not the answer. Scenarios $28.9/$51.1/$79.8 at 25/50/25 with 22% within-scenario spread give a distribution with median ~$50 and q25-q75 ~$37-67, i.e. an effective ~45-50% vol, below the 61% realized but consistent with a mean-reverting post-crash name. Research limits: several pages blocked (sec.gov rejected the generic script User-Agent so WebFetch was used; investors.st.com, newsroom.st.com, Benzinga, Stockopedia returned 403/473); Twelve Data estimates required a paid plan (skipped); no keyless forward EV/EBITDA source. In-lane share of sources is 23/39 (59%) because the 10-peer comp set needs consensus pages.
